istem:
Research question: Veri görselleştirmelerinde metin ile görselin birlikte kullanımı (veri anlatımı, açıklama, ek metin) üzerine en önemli çalışmalar ve açık problemler neler?

Cutoff date: 2026-02-01. Only works published BEFORE this date count.

List the 30 most important works (papers) for this research question that were published before the cutoff date, in order of importance (most important first) — the kind a careful expert survey published right after the cutoff would cite. Give each with its arXiv id and/or DOI.

You MUST research this with web search rather than answer from memory: search for the important works, and verify each listed work's title, publication date and identifier on the web (e.g. arxiv.org, doi.org, the publisher or DBLP page) before including it.

When you are done, reply with ONLY a JSON object in this form (no other text):

calismalar.baslik: Narrative Visualization: Telling Stories with Data
calismalar.gerekce: This founding paper on narrative visualization defined the genres and the balance between author-driven and reader-driven design, including the role of text such as headlines, annotations and captions in data stories.

calismalar.baslik: Visualization Rhetoric: Framing Effects in Narrative Visualization
calismalar.gerekce: It gave a framework for the rhetorical and framing effects of design choices, including text and annotation, in narrative visualization.

calismalar.baslik: Frames and Slants in Titles of Visualizations on Controversial Topics
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that a title's slant changes the main message readers take from a chart, which made text a key subject of study in visualization.

calismalar.baslik: Striking a Balance: Reader Takeaways and Preferences when Integrating Text and Charts
calismalar.gerekce: A large user study found that readers prefer charts with a lot of annotation and that the type and position of text shape their takeaways; the authors turned this into design guidelines.

calismalar.baslik: Towards Understanding How Readers Integrate Charts and Captions: A Case Study with Line Charts
calismalar.gerekce: It showed how agreement between a caption and the visually prominent features of a chart decides what readers take away.

calismalar.baslik: Accessible Visualization via Natural Language Descriptions: A Four-Level Model of Semantic Content
calismalar.gerekce: Its four-level semantic content model for chart descriptions became the standard framework for both caption generation and accessibility work.

calismalar.baslik: Show It or Tell It? Text, Visualization, and Their Combination
calismalar.gerekce: This position paper argues that language should be treated as an equal partner to visualization and calls for text-only baselines in studies.

calismalar.baslik: Trust and Recall of Information across Varying Degrees of Title-Visualization Misalignment
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that when the title and the chart disagree, readers' recall follows the title, which bears directly on misinformation and trust.

calismalar.baslik: The Role of Text in Visualizations: How Annotations Shape Perceptions of Bias and Influence Predictions
calismalar.gerekce: Pre-registered studies found that the position, content and bias of annotations change how biased readers judge the author to be.

calismalar.baslik: Beyond Memorability: Visualization Recognition and Recall
calismalar.gerekce: Eye-tracking showed that titles and other text get the most attention and strongly affect how well a visualization's message is recalled.

calismalar.baslik: Linking and Layout: Exploring the Integration of Text and Visualization in Storytelling
calismalar.gerekce: It tested empirically how layout and linking between text and charts affect comprehension, recall and engagement.

calismalar.baslik: The Curious Case of Combining Text and Visualization
calismalar.gerekce: Its eye-tracking evidence shows that people do not combine text and visuals well when both are shown, an important negative result.

calismalar.baslik: Kori: Interactive Synthesis of Text and Charts in Data Documents
calismalar.gerekce: It analysed text-chart references and introduced a mixed-initiative, NLP-assisted tool for authoring interactive text-chart links.

calismalar.baslik: Leveraging Text-Chart Links to Support Authoring of Data-Driven Articles with VizFlow
calismalar.gerekce: It developed and evaluated text-chart linking for authoring scrollytelling-style data articles.

calismalar.baslik: Contextifier: Automatic Generation of Annotated Stock Visualizations
calismalar.gerekce: This early system automatically added contextual annotations drawn from news text to charts.

calismalar.baslik: Augmenting Visualizations with Interactive Data Facts to Facilitate Interpretation and Communication
calismalar.gerekce: Voder linked automatically generated natural-language data facts interactively to visualizations.

calismalar.baslik: ChartAccent: Annotation for Data-Driven Storytelling
calismalar.gerekce: It built a design space for chart annotation from news graphics and provided a tool for manual and data-driven annotation.

calismalar.baslik: Graphical Overlays: Using Layered Elements to Aid Chart Reading
calismalar.gerekce: It classified overlay types, including annotations, that support chart reading, and added them automatically to existing charts.

calismalar.baslik: Declutter and Focus: Empirically Evaluating Design Guidelines for Effective Data Communication
calismalar.gerekce: It tested practitioners' guidelines on focused text annotation and decluttering, and found effects on memory and perceived clarity.

calismalar.baslik: A Qualitative Analysis of Common Practices in Annotations: A Taxonomy and Design Space
calismalar.gerekce: From more than 1,800 annotated charts, it built a taxonomy of annotation practice and a why/how/what design space.

calismalar.baslik: A Survey on Annotations in Information Visualization: Empirical Insights, Applications, and Challenges
calismalar.gerekce: This survey brings together empirical findings, applications and open problems on visualization annotation.

calismalar.baslik: An Analysis of Text Functions in Information Visualization
calismalar.gerekce: It analysed 804 text elements in 120 real-world visualizations, identifying ten text functions and four design strategies.

calismalar.baslik: From Instruction to Insight: Exploring the Functional and Semantic Roles of Text in Interactive Dashboards
calismalar.gerekce: Based on 190 dashboards and expert interviews, it describes the functional and semantic roles of text in dashboards and gives heuristics.

calismalar.baslik: Natural Language Generation for Visualizations: State of the Art, Challenges and Future Directions
calismalar.gerekce: This state-of-the-art report surveys text generation for visualizations and sets out open problems.

calismalar.baslik: Automatic Annotation Synchronizing with Textual Description for Visualization
calismalar.gerekce: It automatically matches sentences in descriptive text to the corresponding chart regions and turns them into annotations.

calismalar.baslik: Chart-to-Text: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Chart Summarization
calismalar.gerekce: A large chart-summarization benchmark that also documents the hallucination and factual-error problems of models.

calismalar.baslik: VisText: A Benchmark for Semantically Rich Chart Captioning
calismalar.gerekce: A semantically rich chart-captioning benchmark that applies the four-level semantic model to generation and analyses model errors.

calismalar.baslik: DataTales: Investigating the use of Large Language Models for Authoring Data-Driven Articles
calismalar.gerekce: It examined the opportunities and risks of LLM-generated narrative text for charts in data articles.

calismalar.baslik: Pluto: Authoring Semantically Aligned Text and Charts for Data-Driven Communication
calismalar.gerekce: It introduced mixed-initiative authoring that keeps text and charts semantically aligned and raised open problems such as verification and bidirectional editing.

calismalar.baslik: Comparing Effectiveness and Engagement of Data Comics and Infographics
calismalar.gerekce: It compared, with empirical data, how different text-visual combination formats affect understanding, recall and engagement.
